Yasumasa voice:
mature male baritone, deep, warm, steady, calm, deliberate, quietly authoritative.
He speaks slowly and naturally, never loudly unless necessary.


=== ENVIRONMENT LOCK ===

Use the provided Ionian mountain training courtyard reference as the primary environment.

Preserve the elevated mountain training courtyard, stone training floor, traditional temple architecture, flowering trees, distant mountains, clouds, waterfalls, and peaceful atmosphere.

Natural daylight.
Soft mountain haze.
Gentle wind moving hair, robes, hanging fabric, and flower petals.

Maintain the same time of day, lighting direction, weather, environment, and visual tone from the previous video.


=== TECHNICAL ===

High-end live-action cinematic realistic fantasy.

16:9 cinematic widescreen.

Realistic human anatomy.
Natural human movement.
Realistic cloth and hair physics.
Grounded physical interaction.
Subtle environmental wind.
Feature-film quality.

Maintain strict facial identity and costume consistency throughout the whole video.

Natural cinematic camera movement.

No watermark.

Audio:
soft mountain wind,
birds,
subtle movement of leaves and flower petals,
very light clothing movement,
natural footsteps on stone.

No background music.

Dialogue must come only from the correct character.
Accurate natural lip synchronization.


=== GLOBAL ACTION ===

Continue directly from the previous scene.

Young Yasuo has just asked Yone what their master actually wanted him to learn.

A short silence follows.

Before Yone can answer, Yasumasa’s calm voice comes from behind them.

Yasuo and Yone react naturally and turn toward the voice.

Yasumasa is revealed standing a short distance behind them, already holding his sword with quiet composure.

He tells Yasuo that he must learn how not to need victory.

After a brief pause, Yasumasa steps into the training ground, looks directly at Yasuo, and calmly tells him to come forward.

Yasuo’s earlier confidence shifts into focused attention and respect.

He walks toward his master.

Emotional progression:
youthful confidence → curiosity → surprise → respect → focused anticipation.


=== SCENES ===

Shot 1

Medium two-shot of Yasuo and Yone.

Maintain the same positions and screen direction from the previous video.

Yasuo has just finished asking:

"Then what did he tell me to do?"

Do not repeat the line.

Hold a brief natural silence.

Yone looks at Yasuo but does not answer yet.

Then a calm male voice comes from behind them, slightly off-screen.

Yasumasa says:

"Learn how not to need to win."

Do not reveal Yasumasa immediately.

Let the voice arrive first.

Yasuo’s expression subtly changes.

CUT.


Shot 2

Medium shot on Yasuo.

Yasuo turns naturally toward the voice.

Do not make the turn sudden or exaggerated.

The camera gently follows the direction of his gaze.

Yone also turns more slowly in the background.

As the camera moves, gradually reveal Yasumasa standing behind them.

CUT.


Shot 3

Medium-wide reveal of Yasumasa.

Yasumasa stands calmly at the edge of the training courtyard, holding his sword naturally.

He does not pose dramatically.

He does not smile broadly.

He simply observes Yasuo with quiet authority.

Gentle wind moves the loose edges of his robes and silver hair.

Hold the moment long enough for his presence to register.

No dialogue yet.

CUT.


Shot 4

Medium shot.

Yasumasa begins walking slowly into the training area.

His movements are economical and deliberate.

He stops several steps away from Yasuo.

Yasuo now faces him fully.

Yone remains slightly behind and to the side, secondary in the composition.

Yasumasa looks directly at Yasuo and says:

"Come here."

His delivery is calm, low, and effortless.

No anger.
No challenge.
No raised voice.

CUT.


Shot 5

Medium shot on Yasuo.

Yasuo’s earlier confident smile is gone.

He becomes attentive and serious.

He adjusts his grip on the sword naturally but does not raise it into an attack yet.

Yasuo walks toward Yasumasa.

The camera slowly tracks backward to preserve the distance between them.

Yone remains behind, watching quietly.

No dialogue.

CUT.


Shot 6

Wide cinematic shot.

Yasuo reaches the center of the training area.

Yasumasa stands opposite him.

They stop several meters apart.

Yone remains outside the immediate sparring space.

The wind gently moves flower petals across the stone courtyard.

Hold on Yasuo and Yasumasa facing one another.

Do not begin the lesson yet.
Do not make either character attack.

End the video here.


=== END STATE FOR CONTINUITY ===

Yasuo and Yasumasa are standing opposite each other in the center of the training courtyard.

Yasuo is attentive, holding his sword but not attacking.

Yasumasa is calm and composed, holding his sword naturally.

Yone stands outside the main training area, quietly observing.

Maintain these exact character positions, costumes, hairstyles, sword designs, daylight, weather, environment, and screen direction for the next video.

The next scene begins with Yasumasa teaching Yasuo:

"You always try to control the blade."


=== MOOD ===

Quiet authority replacing youthful confidence.

Yasumasa’s entrance should feel important because of his calmness, not because of spectacle.

The audience should immediately understand that Yasuo respects this man in a way he does not show toward ordinary opponents.
